40 In – decay, a neutron inside a nucleus changes to a proton.
Which statement describes the quark composition of the nucleus during the decay?
A
The number of down quarks decreases by one.
B
The number of down quarks increases by one.
C
The number of down quarks stays the same.
D
The number of up quarks stays the same.

hints: Recall the quark make-up of the two nucleons in the question: neutron is $udd$ and proton is $uud$.
In $\beta^-$ decay one $d$ quark changes to a $u$ quark with emission of an electron and antineutrino.
Count $u$ and $d$ quarks before and after to see which total goes up by one and which goes down by one.
walkthrough: Identify the initial and final nucleon: a neutron inside the nucleus changes to a proton.
State the quark model: neutron is $udd$ - one up and two down quarks, proton is $uud$ - two up and one down quarks.
Compare the compositions: up quarks change $1$ to $2$, down quarks change $2$ to $1$.
Interpret the change as one $d$ quark converting to one $u$ quark during $\beta^-$ decay.
Conclude the number of down quarks decreases by one and the number of up quarks increases by one. This is option A.

A.explanation: A neutron $udd$ changing to a proton $uud$ loses one $d$ quark and gains one $u$ quark, so total down quarks decrease by one.

B.explanation: Down quarks do not increase because the $udd$ neutron has two down quarks while the $uud$ proton has only one.

C.explanation: The down quark count cannot stay the same because one $d$ quark changes flavour to $u$ in $\beta^-$ decay.

D.explanation: The up quark count increases from one in the neutron to two in the proton, so it does not stay the same.
